blastocyst.context: A hollow ball of cells with a small clump of inner cells attached to the wall. Used for early embryo development, IVF and stem cell topics.

nucleosome.context: A short stretch of DNA wound around a round histone core like thread on a spool. Used for chromatin, epigenetics and DNA packaging topics.

dna-base-pair.context: Two matching blocks joined by short dashed bonds between two backbone rails. Used for base pairing, nucleotides and DNA structure.

dna-transcription.context: A double helix opening into two strands with a single RNA strand peeling away from the opening. Used for gene expression and transcription topics.

sex-chromosomes.context: A large X shaped chromosome beside a smaller Y shaped chromosome. Used for sex determination, karyotypes and genetics lessons.

dna-methylation.context: A DNA helix with small round tags on short sticks attached at a few points. Used for epigenetics and gene silencing topics.

dna-damage.context: A double helix with one strand snapped and a lightning mark at the break. Used for mutation, radiation and UV damage topics.

dna-repair.context: A double helix with an adhesive bandage patch wrapped diagonally across its middle. Used for DNA repair, gene therapy and healing topics.

supercoiled-dna.context: A looped strand twisted over itself into a tight coil with several crossings. Used for plasmids, DNA topology and topoisomerase topics.

rna-hairpin.context: A single strand folded back on itself with paired rungs and a round loop at the top. Used for RNA secondary structure and stem loop topics.

gene-locus.context: A single chromosome with one highlighted band and an arrow pointing at it. Used for gene mapping and genome browser topics.

operon.context: A straight DNA line with a bent promoter arrow and three gene blocks in a row. Used for bacterial gene regulation lessons.

dna-barcoding.context: A short double helix whose rungs turn into a row of barcode stripes. Used for species identification and DNA testing.

bioinformatics.context: A DNA double helix beside a pair of code brackets. Used for computational biology, genomics software and sequence analysis.

mrna-vaccine.context: A round lipid nanoparticle with a curly RNA strand inside it. Used for vaccine, RNA therapy and immunization topics.

restriction-enzyme.context: A DNA ladder cut by a staggered step break that leaves two overhanging ends. Used for molecular cloning and DNA cutting.

recombinant-dna.context: A small DNA ring with a solid segment inserted at its gap. Used for gene cloning and genetic engineering.

glucose-molecule.context: A six sided sugar ring with one oxygen corner and short hydroxyl sticks. Used for sugar, carbohydrate and blood glucose topics.

fructose-molecule.context: A five sided sugar ring with an oxygen corner and short side sticks. Used for fruit sugar, sweetener and carbohydrate topics.

sucrose-molecule.context: A six sided ring and a five sided ring joined by one bridge. Used for table sugar and disaccharide topics.

polysaccharide.context: A chain of four sugar rings linked end to end in a zigzag. Used for starch, cellulose and glycogen topics.

atp-molecule.context: A base block joined to a five sided sugar ring with a tail of three phosphate dots. Used for cell energy and metabolism topics.

phospholipid.context: A round head with two long tails hanging down, one of them kinked. Used for cell membrane and lipid bilayer topics.

triglyceride.context: A short vertical backbone with three zigzag fatty chains reaching right like the letter E. Used for fat, oil and blood lipid topics.

fatty-acid.context: A long zigzag carbon chain with a small forked carboxyl group at one end. Used for lipid, nutrition and omega 3 topics.

cholesterol-molecule.context: Four fused rings, three six sided and one five sided, with a short tail and a hydroxyl stick. Used for cholesterol, steroid and lipid topics.

heme-group.context: A square ring of four small five sided rings around a central iron dot. Used for hemoglobin, blood and iron topics.

chlorophyll-molecule.context: A ring of four small rings around a central dot with a long wavy tail. Used for photosynthesis and plant pigment topics.

dopamine-molecule.context: A six sided ring with two hydroxyl sticks and a short chain ending in an amine group. Used for neurotransmitter and brain chemistry topics.

serotonin-molecule.context: A six sided ring fused to a five sided ring with a hydroxyl stick and a short chain ending in an amine group. Used for mood and neurotransmitter topics.

insulin-molecule.context: Two short wavy chains, one above the other, linked by two small bridge bars. Used for diabetes, hormone and protein topics.

collagen-triple-helix.context: Three thin strands braided tightly together into a rope. Used for connective tissue, skin and protein topics.

vitamin-c-molecule.context: A five sided ring with a double bond and hydroxyl groups, plus a short side chain with two more hydroxyl groups. Used for ascorbic acid and nutrition topics.

penicillin-molecule.context: A small four sided ring fused to a five sided ring with a side chain and an acid group. Used for antibiotic and drug chemistry topics.

hormone-receptor.context: A cup shaped receptor sitting in a membrane with a small molecule dropping into it. Used for cell signalling and endocrine topics.

antigen.context: A spiky round particle with a Y shaped antibody docking onto its notch. Used for immune response and vaccine topics.

ethanol-molecule.context: Two linked carbon balls with small hydrogen balls around them and an oxygen with its hydrogen at one end. Used for alcohol and organic chemistry topics.

ammonia-molecule.context: A central nitrogen ball with three hydrogen balls splayed below like a tripod. Used for fertilizer, cleaning and chemistry lessons.

ozone-molecule.context: Three oxygen balls joined in a bent V shape. Used for ozone layer and atmosphere topics.

hydrogen-peroxide-molecule.context: Two joined oxygen balls with a hydrogen ball on each end, twisted like an open book. Used for bleach, antiseptic and oxidizer topics.

sulfuric-acid-molecule.context: A central sulfur ball with four oxygen balls around it, two of them capped by small hydrogen balls. Used for acid and industrial chemistry topics.

ethylene-molecule.context: Two carbon balls joined by a double bar with two hydrogen balls on each end. Used for alkene, plant hormone and plastics topics.

acetic-acid-molecule.context: A two carbon skeleton with a doubled oxygen at the upper right and a hydroxyl oxygen at the lower right. Used for vinegar and carboxylic acid topics.

naphthalene.context: Two six sided rings fused side by side sharing one edge, with inner double bond lines. Used for aromatic hydrocarbon and mothball topics.

cyclopentane-ring.context: A single five sided ring skeletal formula with a small carbon dot at each corner. Used for cycloalkane and organic chemistry topics.

graphite-structure.context: Three flat slanted sheets stacked in parallel layers. Used for carbon allotrope, graphene and pencil lead topics.

ferrocene.context: An iron atom dot sandwiched between two flat five sided rings, one above and one below. Used for organometallic and sandwich compound topics.

dendrimer.context: A central dot with branches that fork again and again outward like a round snowflake tree. Used for branched polymer and nanotechnology topics.

rotaxane.context: A dumbbell shaped rod with a big stopper at each end and a ring threaded around its middle. Used for molecular machines and supramolecular chemistry.

cross-linked-polymer.context: Three parallel wavy chains joined at intervals by short bridge bonds. Used for rubber, gels and plastics topics.

tetrahedral-molecule.context: A central atom with four bonds pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron, one wedge and one dashed. Used for molecular geometry and stereochemistry lessons.

octahedral-molecule.context: A central atom with six bonds along three crossing axes, each ending in a dot. Used for coordination chemistry and molecular geometry lessons.

trigonal-planar-molecule.context: A central atom with three bonds spread evenly at 120 degrees on a flat plane. Used for molecular geometry and VSEPR lessons.

space-filling-model.context: Four overlapping spheres fused into one lumpy molecule shape. Used for molecular models and van der Waals surface topics.

dipole-molecule.context: A bent three ball molecule with a crossed arrow below showing the direction of the dipole. Used for polarity and water chemistry topics.

ion-atom.context: A round atom with a nucleus, an orbit with electrons and a bold plus sign. Used for cation, charge and ionization topics.

free-radical.context: A small two ball molecule with a single unpaired dot beside it and a small spark. Used for oxidative stress and antioxidant topics.

polymerization.context: Single small units on the left turning into a linked chain on the right with an arrow between. Used for plastics and polymer chemistry topics.

resonance-structures.context: Two six sided rings with their inner bonds swapped, joined by a double headed arrow. Used for benzene and delocalization lessons.

cis-trans-isomers.context: Two double bond molecules, one with both marked groups on the same side and one with them on opposite sides. Used for stereoisomer lessons.

entropy.context: A neat grid of dots on the left and the same dots scattered randomly on the right, with an arrow between. Used for disorder and thermodynamics topics.

salt-bridge.context: An inverted U shaped tube joining the tops of two beakers. Used for electrochemical cells and galvanic cell lessons.

gram-stain.context: A glass slide holding small round and rod shaped cells with a stain drop falling from above. Used for bacteria identification in microbiology labs.

coplin-jar.context: A small upright glass jar with a lid and several microscope slides standing inside. Used for staining slides in histology and microbiology.

cell-spreader.context: A thin rod bent into an L shape, spreading liquid across an open petri dish. Used for plating bacteria on agar.

serial-dilution.context: A row of three test tubes, each holding less liquid than the last, with curved arrows between them. Used for dilution series in microbiology and chemistry.

colony-counter.context: A petri dish with several colony dots under a magnifying lens. Used for counting bacterial colonies.

replica-plating.context: A round velvet covered stamp pressed down onto a petri dish with colony dots. Used for transferring colonies between plates.

pipette-controller.context: A pistol grip pipette gun with a long thin graduated pipette fitted at the front. Used for liquid handling in cell culture and microbiology.

cell-scraper.context: A long handle ending in a small angled flat blade, like a tiny squeegee. Used for harvesting adherent cells in tissue culture.

dounce-homogenizer.context: A tall narrow glass tube with a round ended glass pestle plunged inside it. Used for grinding tissue and breaking cells.

cell-strainer.context: A small mesh cup sitting on top of the opening of a conical tube. Used for filtering cell suspensions.

syringe-filter.context: A small round disc filter fitted on the tip of a syringe, with a drop falling below. Used for sterile filtering of lab samples.

heat-block.context: A flat metal block with tubes standing in its holes and a temperature display on the front. Used for warming samples in a lab.

flow-cytometry.context: A thin stream carrying single round cells in a line through a laser beam, with a detector beside it. Used for cell counting and sorting.

nanopore-sequencing.context: A single DNA strand threading through a small pore in a membrane band, with a signal line below. Used for long read DNA sequencing.

dna-sequencing-trace.context: A row of sharp overlapping peaks with a dot above each one marking the called base. Used for Sanger sequencing results.

elisa-well.context: A cutaway of a single well with antibodies on the bottom, a captured antigen and a glowing tag on top. Used for immunoassay and antibody test topics.

pcr-tube-strip.context: A row of small conical tubes joined in a strip with connected caps along the top. Used for PCR and molecular biology labs.

spin-column.context: A small column with a filter disc standing in a larger microtube, with a curved spin arrow. Used for DNA extraction and purification kits.
